Day done at The National.

We’re walking back to the hotel, and I couldn’t stop thinking about one card…

The 1986 Fleer Michael Jordan rookie.

Don’t get me wrong. It’s one of the most iconic cards ever made. But the more I thought about it, the more one question kept coming back.

Who’s buying all of them?

There are now more than 26,000 PSA-graded copies in the PSA population report, including thousands of PSA 8s and PSA 9s, yet the card continues to command strong prices because collector demand for Jordan has remained incredibly deep.

I’m not saying it’s overrated.

I’m just trying to understand why demand keeps absorbing such a massive supply.

Maybe I’m looking at it the wrong way.

What am I missing?

Would you buy a 1986 Fleer Jordan at today’s prices, or would you put that money into something else?

Follow along for more conversations from the hobby.

⸻

Convince me.

If the population keeps growing, why do you think the 1986 Fleer Jordan continues to hold its value?

A guy walked up to my table at the Columbus Card Fest and we got to talking about the hobby. He told me he doesn’t work a regular job anymore… buying and selling Sports Cards is all he does.

Then the conversation took a turn I wasn’t expecting.

We started talking about building a personal collection, and he looked at me and said, “Nobody should build a PC. Just keep buying and selling.”

I’ll be honest… I don’t know if I agree.

For me, part of this hobby has always been owning a few cards that actually mean something. Sure, I love making deals and turning inventory, but not every card has to be for sale.

That conversation stuck with me because it really makes you think about why you’re in this hobby in the first place.

Are you here to invest?
To collect?
To flip?
Or maybe a little of all three?

I’m curious where everyone stands on this one.

🦁1 of 1 Impeccable Dual Auto of Barry Sanders & Calvin Johnson🦁 

A grail type Lions card. Obviously would be incredible if they weren’t sticker autos, but it’s a licensed & pack-pulled card. And they just simply don’t have many dual autos at all. Even this set there’s only 26 total copies. The “base” auto is out of 25 and then there’s the 1 of 1. 

Nice images of each & also bold signatures. This will be coming to Shipshewana with me (probably with a crazy price tag 🤣). The perfect card for me to hold onto forever unless the right number comes along. Go Lions! 

#barrysanders #calvinjohnson #detroitlions #nfl #football

Incredible time today at the Detroit Sports Spectacular getting to meet Jake Bates, Aidan Hutchinson & Jared Goff! All seemed like great guys, which made the experience even better as a huge Lions fan. Pumped to add all of these into my PC. All are 1 of 1’s — I know some have mixed feelings on getting those signed in person. In this case I didn’t mind anyway because they are PC, but I absolute think it can add to the value of certain cards.

The Bates IMO is easily his best card & will remain that way. Wasn’t in any actual sets. Has a few different panini instant cards and no on-card autos. This being a 1/1 and now an on card auto with a unique inscription. I’m sure he’ll eventually be in a Prizm or select set and the black 1 of 1 or nebulas would do quite well, which would only help a piece like this. Would be really fun if he could stick as a long-time Lion! Had a historically great rookie year. We’ve had some really good kickers in Detroit over the years. Jake is more talented than all of them. 

The Hutch is right up there for the favorite card in my collection. In my favorite Lions unis (throwbacks), has a cool image of him intercepting a pass, and the black ink really pops here! Also was interesting to learn from Hutch that with his fanatics exclusive deal he can’t inscribe cards or sign any with his “A” auto. On other items he includes a big capital A but for cards you’ll notice it’s only always his “Hutch” looking auto. Really great guy. For as big of a star as he is he stood out to me as being unbelievably personable and nice to his fans. 

Goff was also a very nice guy! His crew really was making sure the line went by, but he still chatted with everyone and took a lot of time signing his auto. Also made some funny comments about how well certain autos were coming out after he signed it. Could tell he cared to do a nice job for people and was telling younger collectors to make sure to let the ink dry so it wouldn’t smudge. I’ll have to have him sign a better card if he comes next year, but I do really like the black jerseys and a 1 of 1 from his 18-for-18 game is still a pretty awesome card!

Ended 1 half too soon, but my first season as a @detroitlionsnfl season ticket holder couldn’t have gone much better. Had a blast & can’t wait for next year. 🦁 

#Goff4MVP #OrangeCards🍊

1985 Star Lite All-Stars Michael Jordan #4 Rookie Card BGS Authentic 🍺 🏀 🐐 

I was so excited to be able to acquire this card at the August 2026 @shipshewanacardfest! Truly one I didn’t think I’d be walking out of the show with, but I was able to make it happen. This copy has a lot to offer with very strong left to right centering, bold blue coloring and a very nice & centered back. 

The Miller Lite & Gatorade Star are by far my favorite Jordan cards. Love the branding & coloring of the beverages being prominent on the card, and the cards being event-exclusive to the 1985 NBA All-Star Weekend. Also for Michael Jordan it’s very cool IMO that a licensed card was issued during his actual rookie season. This card was issued 18 months prior to 1986 Fleer & is approximately 50 times more rare (4K print run compared to 200K ish). 

Thank you very much to @bad_boyz_collectibles for bringing such an awesome card to show & being very fair and negotiable on the price. This was a huge purchase for me and they were great to work with, which is fitting for the type of family-oriented / first-class show @bee_sports runs.

#starbasketballcards #starjordan #michaeljordan #nba

1986 Star Michael Jordan #8 — The 1986 Playoffs 🟥🏀 

My lone pick up from my 1 day at the 2026 National! The show was a great time & I am thrilled to add my first 1986 Jordan card. The bright neon-ish coloring of the Star cards is what initially drew me into these sets. I think I found some great value in this copy because the vibrant coloring is present here along with crisp corners and edges. I didn’t mind sacrificing the centering for that reason. Another interesting element to this card is that the graded pop for all Beckett grades is only 1100 (PSA still doesn’t grade this set) compared to the significantly higher pop of the Fleer.

The three individuals who broke into Bridgeport Hobby.

It genuinely hurts my heart seeing this continue to happen to shops all over the hobby.

These aren’t just stores. They’re people’s livelihoods. Years of hard work, sacrifice, and risk go into building these places. For a lot of collectors, their local shop is also a place to escape for a little bit, talk cards, see friends, and be part of a community.

We’ll recover. We’ll tighten security and come back stronger. I’m more concerned about making sure this doesn’t keep happening to the next shop.

If you own a shop, please take security seriously and check every possible weak point. We never imagined someone would come through an AC unit until it happened to us.

Look out for each other. Shops shouldn’t have to keep going through this.

Bridgeport Hobby isn’t going anywhere. ❤️

Love,
Rob

Here’s the video of the burglary.

In less than 3 minutes, roughly $50,000 in inventory was taken from our shop.

This is obviously a big hit for us as a small business, especially while we’re working on opening @grailcardboard next door. But more than anything, this whole situation has made me think about the safety of our customers, our team, and the community we’ve built here.

Bridgeport Hobby has always been more than a card shop to me. For a lot of us, this hobby is a break from reality. It’s a place to hang out, talk cards, trade, collect, and be around people who share the same passion. I want everyone who walks through our doors to always feel safe here.

We started a GoFundMe (link in bio) to help us recover and strengthen the security of the shop so we can do everything possible to make sure something like this doesn’t happen again.

Please don’t feel obligated to donate. Sharing this, stopping by the shop, or simply continuing to support us means just as much.

If we raise more than what we need, every dollar left over will go toward helping other small businesses in Bridgeport and other card shops to strengthen their security. I hate that this has happened to us, as well as many other shops, but if something positive can come from it by helping prevent another shop from going through the same thing, I want to do that.

And to every other shop owner, please check every possible weak point in your building. I never would have thought someone could get into ours through an AC unit.

Thank you to everyone who has reached out, donated, shared, stopped by, or just checked in on us. The support has genuinely meant a lot to me and everyone here.

We’re going to fix what needs to be fixed, keep moving forward, and make sure Bridgeport Hobby continues to be the safe place and escape it has always been for so many of us.

Love you guys. Thank you.

— Rob
